findings_qualitative.value: Total gas (H2+HI) is normal for stellar mass, suggesting efficient HI to H2 conversion by ram pressure

evidence.quote: the total gas (molecular+neutral) associated to our jellyfish galaxies (considering both what is left in the disk and what is in the tail) is normal for their stellar mass

claims.hypothesis: Jellyfish galaxies have molecular gas content like normal galaxies
claims.experiment: CO(1-0) ALMA H2 masses vs xCOLDGASS
claims.finding: Jellyfish disks are H2 rich unless alpha_CO is very low

evidence.quote: jellyfish galaxies have huge reservoirs of $H_2$

claims.hypothesis: Ram pressure efficiently converts HI into H2
claims.experiment: Rmol and total gas fraction vs normal spirals

evidence.quote: the gas compression caused by the ram pressure in the peak stripping phase causes the conversion of large amounts of HI into the molecular phase

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Ram pressure unbinding GMCs gives lower alpha_CO; tested with Amorin2016 formulation

evidence.quote: ram-pressure acting on the infalling galaxies could in principle unbind the already existing giant molecular clouds (GMCs) in the galaxy disk

limitations_admitted.value: No single-dish CO(1-0) data so fluxes are lower limits

evidence.quote: We do not have single dish data at the CO(1-0) frequency to assess the possible flux loss, and therefore our data are, strictly speaking, lower limits.
